definition: Forbearance means patience and self-restraint when provoked.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word forbearance. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know forbearance should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Mrs. Idowu bore the trumpet practice next door with a forbearance that never once curdled into a complaint.
Politeness is the mildest rung, well below forbearance — you can be perfectly polite to a customer who has done nothing to try you, while forbearance only begins once real provocation lands.
Patience goes further than politeness — it stays calm through long delays — but patience is tested by time, while forbearance is tested by insult.

Restraint is holding yourself back from any impulse at all — spending, bragging, the second dessert. Forbearance is restraint of one particular kind: you have been provoked, the sharp reply is ready and deserved, and you hold it back and stay kind anyway.

Tolerance is putting up with what you dislike — noise, habits, opinions — often by simply deciding it is not your business. Forbearance is more personal and harder won: the provocation is aimed at you, it stings, and you still choose not to answer the sting in kind.

Composure is the steady surface — the level voice and unshaken face a person keeps under stress, with no promise about what happens next. Forbearance goes past appearances: provoked and stung, you not only stay steady but choose not to answer the insult at all.

Idowu bore the trumpet practice next door with a forbearance that never once curdled into a complaint.

For eleven years the bookshop's loudest regular has mispronounced every author he buys, brought paperbacks back half-read with the spines cracked, and lectured the owner on stocking 'real literature.' She bears it all with forbearance: she trades the damaged copies out, recommends his next book, and has never once told him what she thinks of his manners.
Forbearance is the exact word for the owner's restraint, because forbearance means patience and self-restraint when provoked — and the provocation is standing at her register, weekly.
Patience alone is tested by delay; forbearance is tested by insult, and it holds anyway.
Forbearance is the grown-up of the patience family: it holds steady while being provoked, and it chooses not to answer in kind.
Its unit-mates work nearby — lenient softens the punishment an authority hands down, tactful takes the wounding words out of a sentence, accommodating rearranges plans.
Forbearance simply absorbs the sting and stays kind.

Okonjo's hardware store opened at seven, and for eleven years Harold Voss arrived at five past to explain what was wrong with it.
The new awning, Voss announced to the whole checkout line, made the block look like a circus.
Okonjo's nephew, who worked summers at the register, kept a list of the comebacks his uncle never used.
The old man heard each jab, let a beat pass, and asked after Voss's tomatoes — a forbearance so complete the regulars mistook it for deafness.
When Voss was snowed in one February, it was Okonjo who shoveled his walk.
